records.issue_text: .env.example CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY comment claims 32 bytes for AES256 but suggests generating with `openssl rand -base64 24`, which produces only 24 bytes
records.rationale: The diff adds '# must be 32 bytes for AES256 encryption algorithm' followed by '# You can use: `openssl rand -base64 24`' — base64-encoding 24 random bytes yields a 24-byte key, contradicting the stated 32-byte requirement. This key feeds symmetricDecrypt for AES256, so following the suggested command would produce a key of the wrong length, breaking credential sync at runtime.
records.stripped_text: .env.example CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY comment claims 32 bytes for AES256 but suggests generating with `openssl rand -base64 24`, which produces only 24 bytes

records.issue_text: CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is added out of alphabetical order in turbo.json's env var list, breaking the existing sorting convention
records.rationale: The finding is a pure alphabetical-ordering nit in turbo.json. While factually true that CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET appears after CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY, this is a cosmetic style/preference concern with no functional consequence; also the diff already inserts CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME out of strict order, showing no strict convention. Per the rules, pure style nits are hallucination-grade.
records.stripped_text: CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is added out of alphabetical order in turbo.json's env var list, breaking the existing sorting convention

records.issue_text: Office365 CalendarService removed console.error logging on zod parse failure while parseRefreshTokenResponse now throws on schema mismatch, and the throw isn't caught, causing a potential unhandled rejection instead of graceful degradation
records.rationale: The diff confirms the mechanism: parseRefreshTokenResponse does `throw new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` on failure, while the office365 caller previously did `if (!tokenResponse.success) { console.error(...) }` and continued; that graceful handling is deleted in this diff, so a malformed token response now raises an unhandled exception in refreshAccessToken. This is a real behavior change verifiable from the diff, though severity (whether surrounding code catches it) is not fully visible.
records.stripped_text: Office365 CalendarService removed console.error logging on zod parse failure while parseRefreshTokenResponse now throws on schema mismatch, and the throw isn't caught, causing a potential unhandled rejection instead of graceful degradation

records.issue_text: Salesforce CalendarService refresh-token fetch runs unconditionally on every getConnection()/instantiation instead of only when the token is expired, causing an unnecessary network round-trip and OAuth refresh on every use
records.rationale: The diff adds a fetch to Salesforce's login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token in the getConnection flow before `return new jsforce.Connection({...})`, with no expiry/refresh check — the fetch, parse, and prisma.credential.update run unconditionally on every instantiation, unlike the other services which gate refresh behind token expiry checks. This is a real, verifiable defect introduced by this diff (extra network round-trip and DB write on every use).
records.stripped_text: Salesforce CalendarService refresh-token fetch runs unconditionally on every getConnection()/instantiation instead of only when the token is expired, causing an unnecessary network round-trip and OAuth refresh on every use

records.issue_text: Webhook endpoint lacks rate limiting, allowing iterative brute-forcing of the secret and writing arbitrary encrypted credentials for any userId/appSlug pair
records.rationale: The new handler in apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts performs a single equality check of a header against CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET with no rate limiting or lockout visible anywhere in the diff, and on success writes credential keys for arbitrary userId/appSlug. The mechanism described is consistent with the code shown; whether maintainers consider missing rate limiting a shippable defect is somewhat judgment-dependent.
records.stripped_text: Webhook endpoint lacks rate limiting, allowing iterative brute-forcing of the secret and writing arbitrary encrypted credentials for any userId/appSlug pair
